Il lessico BI-RADS per l'ecografia descr:
The BI-RADS ultrasound lexicon describes a mass with a few words: shape (oval, round, irregular), orientation (parallel to the skin = wider than tall; not parallel = taller than wide), margins (circumscribed, or indistinct, angular, microlobulated, spiculated), echo pattern (anechoic, hypoechoic, complex…) and posterior features (enhancement, shadowing, none).
Not every BI-RADS 4 lesion is a tumour: the category means that tissue sampling is needed, and many BI-RADS 4 biopsies turn out benign.
After every biopsy the radiologist checks concordance: does the result explain the appearance of the lesion? An intraductal papilloma explains an irregular solid mass, but it is a B3 lesion (uncertain potential): a needle biopsy may miss atypia or papillary carcinoma. This is why it is often excised.
Papilloma sometimes causes serous or bloody nipple discharge: in that case look for a lesion in the retroareolar ducts.
Dopo la biopsia: istologia e immagini de: After biopsy: pathology and imaging must agree; papillary lesions are discussed.
